html:
SMTO-SKL-0102 — Microsoft 365 couldn't find that item

GUID: be5bf6b9-dfcf-5895-be5a-d2027e619e47
Slug: microsoft365-resource-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • The item SMTO asked for isn't where it was expected in this Microsoft account. It may have been moved or deleted, or it belongs to a different account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to search for the item again by name, subject or date in the same account. A fresh search finds the item's current location if it was moved.
  2. Check in Outlook or OneDrive that the item still exists and wasn't deleted. If it was deleted, there's nothing for SMTO to open.
  3. If you have more than one Microsoft account connected, tell the Agent which account holds the item. An item in one account can't be found from another.

What success looks like

  • The Agent finds the item and shows its details.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft Graph returned HTTP 404 or ErrorItemNotFound for the requested resource, before a mail, event, contact or file-specific not-found translation applied.

What this means

  • Graph returns HTTP 404 or ErrorItemNotFound before a more specific service family translation. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Graph returns HTTP 404 or ErrorItemNotFound before a more specific service family translation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact route, identity and access; the response does not prove deletion.

How to fix it

  • Re-list or search with the same account_ref to get a current resource ID, and use that exact ID. Do not substitute another account or tenant; IDs can change when items move between folders or drives.
  • Read/search the same account again and use an exact current resource ID; do not substitute another account or tenant.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • An authorized same-account read resolves the intended resource.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
